idle: We need cones at the far end. We means you.
Sixty volunteers and a freezer of squares. We're fine.
good_ice: That's ice I'd put a six-year-old on.
bad_ice: A rut at the blue line. I've seen it. I've written it down.
cold: Cold. Somebody find the heater for the parents.
long_line: Four teams in two dressing rooms. We'll make it work. You'll make it work.
leaving_happy: Good morning on the ice. Thank the driver, kids!
leaving_angry: I'll be in touch. In writing.

minor_hockey: Keep your stick on the ice, Owen!
Who's coaching from the glass? Rick. It's always Rick.
tournament: Five towns, eighty families, one canteen. Brace yourselves.
learn_to_skate: Look at that. She let go of the boards. Don't cry, Donna.

first.say: Donna Pettigrew, Minor Hockey. I moved half our ice to Harlow Falls last spring. I'd like to move it back. Convince me.

options.text: The ice is getting better, I promise.

first_need.say: Safe ice. Two dressing rooms that lock. An AED on the wall. Saturday mornings at the capped rate. We'll start there.

first_promise.say: Promises don't hold up a six-year-old. Ice does.

say: A rut at the blue line on Saturday. A seven-year-old went down. He's fine. I'm not.

options.text: I'm sorry. It won't happen again.

grumpy_bad.say: Kids fall on good ice. On bad ice they get hurt. Write that on your wall.

practice.say: Look at them. Thirty mittens and one puck. We need cones at the far end, {owner}.

options.text: Is that a parent coaching from the glass?

rick.say: Rick Saucier. Every week. I've drafted a letter. Then a second letter about the first letter.

tourney.say: Valley Peewee weekend. Five towns, eighty families, one canteen. We're going to need Lorraine at full power.

say: {owner}. The squares are in the office. Lemon. Don't tell the U9 parents.
There you are. We have a list. You'll like it. You won't.
Donna Pettigrew. I have four minutes.

options.text: What do you think of Priya?
How's the ice for the kids?
Any notes on my team, boss?
Your ice rate and my club. Two hats.

job.say: Two hundred kids, sixty volunteers, one bake sale freezer. We run on squares and stubbornness.

options.text: How much ice did you move to Harlow Falls?

hf.say: Half. They have a 'Pathway to Excellence' poster. Our pathway has a bake sale. Give me a reason to bring it home.

events.say: Minor hockey, obviously. The tournament. And learn to skate, when a kid lets go of the boards for the first time. Don't tell anyone that's my favourite.

priya.say: Priya answers on the second ring and sends invoices on the first. I'd hire her if I could afford her.

helene.say: She wants 06:00. I want 06:00. One of us coaches figure skating. We're civil.

options.text: Good enough to bring the kids home?

rink_home.say: Close. I'm bringing the U11s back in January. Don't make me regret it.

do.note: Donna Pettigrew is bringing the U11s back from Harlow Falls in January.

rink_rooms.say: Two rooms that lock and a drain that works. The parents noticed. Parents notice everything except their own kids' mouthguards.

rink_need.say: An AED by the door, ice without ruts, and nobody cancelling Saturday six a.m. by text.

coach.say: Your kids pass. Your bench doesn't. And thank the Zambelli driver after practice. Every time.

gm.say: If you give your own club my Saturday, I'll know. Everybody will know. Wear both hats where we can see them.
